title: Stocks After Every Midterm Since 1950: 19 for 19 #shorts
description:
Every US midterm election since 1950, the S&P 500 was higher one year later: 19 out of 19.

Average gain: about 15% (+15.1%). Worst: +1.1% (1986). Best: +33.2% (1954).

How we measured it: S&P 500 closing price on election day (or the last trading day before it, since markets used to close on election day) versus the close on the same date one year later, for all 19 midterms from 1950 to 2022. Price only, dividends not included. Source: S&P 500 index (^GSPC) daily closes via Yahoo Finance; our calculation.

This is history, not a prediction. Small sample, and past results don't guarantee future returns. This video doesn't take a side in the election.

Full video: What the midterms could mean for your money https://youtu.be/37Aow08f8zk

This video is for education only and is not financial advice.
Original script and animation; stock footage from Canva. Narrated with an AI voice.
